key_insight: Compatible sparse-grid finite elements for BGG complexes achieve dimension-independent convergence rates in degrees of freedom under mixed Sobolev regularity assumptions.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports efficient, stable discretizations of elasticity and higher-order mechanics problems while reducing full-grid computational costs.
method: Build compatible polynomial hierarchies from Alpert wavelets and their first and second primitives.
Construct tensor-product sparse-grid BGG finite elements.
Use a bounded commuting projection to establish stable discrete potentials for Hessian, elasticity, and div-div complexes.
evidence_signal: Experiments on a 3D incompatibility problem and a 2D biharmonic problem on an annulus illustrate efficiency relative to full grids.
watch_item: The approximation guarantees require mixed Sobolev regularity, which should be checked for problems with singularities or nonsmooth solutions.
